thread:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT: #4971 - GPU capacity alarm triggered in eu-west-1 (prod). queue_length > 95% for 5m, throttles increasing. auto-escalation to oncall.

maria: acked. i'm oncall for this window, starting triage. can someone pull the autoscaler metrics and recent deploys?

jamal: looking at autoscaler logs now. API shows scale requests fired but kube autoscaler returned 'limitReached'. maxReplicaCount hit on the gpu-pool (configured 18).

oliver: confirmed. pool reported 18/18 provisioned, each at ~98% GPU util. queue growth correlates with a spike in small, high-qps requests around 14:05 UTC.

katie: CS note: a couple of customers are reporting 429s and higher tail latency on chat endpoints. no big P0 customer yet but multiple mid-market tenants impacted.

maria: interesting — any recent config changes to batching or cache? that often changes packing efficiency.

jamal: checking change history... i see a config push at 13:58 by rollout-bot: "adjust continuous_batch.window_ms from 8 -> 25" and "prefix_cache.ttl from 300s -> 30s" for model-profile redwood-llama-v1.

oliver: that matches a drop in pack_factor on the runtime. after 13:58 average tokens-per-invocation packing dropped ~40%. more small payloads with less effective batching -> fewer long-lived KV cache hits.

sre-lead: tagging: this looks like a regression where increasing batch window actually increased latency for single-request flows and reduced batching efficiency for our workload. prefix_cache TTL drop explains cache missstorm.

maria: good catch. we need immediate mitigations: (1) raise pool maxReplicaCount to 30 (manual scale) (2) rollback the 13:58 config change for continuous_batch and prefix_cache (3) apply an emergency prefix_cache.hot-ttl to 600 for hot keys, if rollback takes time.

infra-bot: runbook command executed: `kubectl scale --replicas=30 deploy/gpu-pool-eu-west1` returned 202 accepted. new pods scheduled, ETA ~6m.

jamal: starting rollback of feature flag for batch/cache via infra-config (can target traffic-plane only, no model change). patch submitted.

maria: i'm going to throttle non-urgent background inference routes at the proxy layer to create headroom for low-latency customer traffic. @katie please update CS with mitigation plan.

katie: on it — DMing affected accounts w/ ETA. will post a short status update in #customers-affected.

oliver: logs show a lot of prefix_cache misses for common prompts; hit ratio dropped from 82% to 18% after TTL change. KV cache churn is causing higher memory pressure too.

sre-lead: note: scaling now will buy capacity but doesn't fix packing inefficiency. rollback is higher priority to restore pack factor.

jamal: rollback applied at 14:18 UTC. continuous_batch.window_ms -> 8, prefix_cache.ttl -> 300. rollout reported successful on 3/3 nodes.

maria: monitoring pack_factor and queue. pack_factor recovering — 14:22 it jumped from 0.6 -> 1.1 avg tokens-per-call. queue length decreasing.

pagerduty-bot: STATUS CHANGE: #4971 -> acknowledged -> identified.

oliver: after rollback, we still see some cascade of requests where clients retried and flooded the queue. i'm throttling retry-backoff to 2s at edge. also enabling short token-burst damping.

infra-bot: new pool replicas are ready: 12 of 12 (manual scale). autoscaler remains capped at 18 until we bump maxReplicaCount in config.

maria: ops decision: leave manual scale at 30 for now, we'll revert to autoscaler after we confirm stable pack rates and tail latency. need a config change to bump maxReplicaCount for the autoscaler to 40; i'll open change request.

katie: sent CS update: "We've rolled back a recent batching/cache config change and added capacity. Some customers may see reduced errors in the next 5-10 minutes. We're monitoring and will follow up." :thumbsup: 

oliver: metrics: 95th latency dropped from 1.8s -> 0.7s within 10m of rollback, token cost per request normalized. cache hit ratio climbing.

sre-lead: good. root cause hypothesis for postmortem: bad config tweak to continuous batching and aggressive TTL reduction caused packing regression + prefix cache missstorm. that combo reduced effective throughput and pushed pool to autoscaler ceiling.

maria: action items (short):
- roll back batching/prefix cache change (done)
- keep manual scale at 30 until end of incident (done)
- open autoscaler config PR to bump maxReplicaCount -> 40 (jamal)
- add deploy-gate to prevent simultaneous batching+cache param changes in the same rollout (oliver)
- add a runtime regression alert for pack_factor drop > 30% in 5m (sre-lead)
- post incident note to customers + include mitigation steps (katie)

jamal: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/PR-8345 (bump maxReplicaCount + tests).

pagerduty-bot: STATUS CHANGE: #4971 -> mitigated.

maria: handing off to @oliver for on-call follow-up and postmortem. i'm going offline for the shift change in 35m.

oliver: ack. i'll collect logs, attach sampling of requests that missed prefix cache, and schedule PM for postmortem with ML infra and runtime.

cs-ops: noted. will hold customer-facing write-up until postmortem summary approved.

maria: thanks team. final note: unlike previous pool-exhaustion incidents this was primarily a config regression, not autoscaler bug. still want a safety valve in autoscaler to allow emergency burst above maxReplicaCount when queue growth rate > X. adding to backlog. :white_check_mark: 

pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT #4971 closed at 14:29:59 UTC (status: resolved, duration: 24m 47s).
